represents: About an hour (the v2 expansion spans 58 minutes) of det-eng-keyed syscalls on a developer/admin workstation (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, GNOME on Wayland, Firefox snap, Docker Engine with runc 1.1): GPU/tty ioctls, shell pipelines, git/ssh/make/gcc/go/cargo/python/node/VS Code, systemd and snap-confine cgroup-BPF loads, resolved/NetworkManager/sshd/sudo/apt, memfd shared memory (Firefox, PipeWire, mutter, Xwayland), a docker-proxy splicing a local Postgres/Redis port, docker exec/run through runc; plus admin and debugging work adjacent to the rules: gdb/dlv/strace, perf and async-profiler, bpftool and bcc execsnoop, tcpdump, ping/tracepath/mtr, `ip xfrm` and strongSwan charon-nm, `ip netns add/exec`, `unshare -rn`, systemd PrivateNetwork units, `cryptsetup open` of a LUKS2 backup disk (AF_ALG + kernel keyring), `keyctl show`, fio with io_uring. Template weights set which behaviours appear and roughly how often relative to each other, not their production call rates: a real fio io_uring run issues thousands of io_uring_enter calls a second where this slice has a handful, and a busy docker-proxy splices far more. Treat hits and rate_per_10k as presence indicators (does this benign behaviour trip the rule, and by which actor), not as production false-positive rates.
provenance: synthetic; event shape = detections/validate_detections.py normalize() output for SYSCALL records keyed det-eng; only syscalls in detections/audit/atomic.rules; argument encodings from the syscall ABIs (socket family/type/protocol incl. SOCK_CLOEXEC/NONBLOCK bits, setsockopt level/optname, ioctl request numbers from asm-generic/ioctls.h, sockios.h, dm-ioctl.h and drm.h, bpf(2) command numbers, ptrace(2) requests, unshare/setns CLONE_* flags, memfd_create MFD_* flags), and documented tool behaviour (iputils ping datagram ICMP, libpcap TPACKET setup, iproute2 netlink options, gdb/Go PTRACE_TRACEME in the forked inferior, strace PTRACE_SEIZE + GET_SYSCALL_INFO, Go's splice pipe pool (pipe2 O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK), runc 1.1's memfd re-exec and nsexec stage names, snap-confine's device-cgroup BPF and preserved mount namespace, cryptsetup LUKS2 AF_ALG keyslot decryption and logon key). Pointer arguments are random addresses in the right regions; pids are fixed for daemons and drawn per tool session. int -1 arguments are logged as 32-bit ffffffff, as glibc's variadic syscall() passes an int. Multi-syscall behaviour is written as sequences that share one draw (same pid, milliseconds apart), so correlation rules see it as it happens: runc 1.1's memfd re-exec on every container start (runc init, comm exe: memfd_create(MFD_CLOEXEC|MFD_ALLOW_SEALING), then ~40 ms later execveat(fd, "", AT_EMPTY_PATH) whose record already carries the new image's comm (the fd number) and exe (the memfd)), followed by nsexec's runc:[1:CHILD] (cloned with CLONE_PARENT, so a child of the runc create/exec process) setns()ing into each namespace (docker exec) or unsharing new ones, with runc:[2:INIT] unsharing the cgroup namespace and runc loading, querying and attaching its cgroup-v2 device filter (docker run); and docker-proxy's Go splice path on a new connection with an empty pipe pool (socket to the backend, then per direction pipe2 and two splices through that pipe). Everything else is drawn independently. comm/exe values are in normalize() output form: auditd hex-encodes a comm or exe containing a space, and normalize() decodes it, so they read as plain text.
